clue.text: The leftist full of beans is spurned

indicators.note: full of means the word for leftist holds the word for beans inside it

parts.note: a red is a left-winger
pulses are edible seeds such as beans and lentils

explanation.surface: Someone is told that the energetic left-winger has been rejected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Full of beans' looks like the idiom for lively, but here 'full of' is a container signal and beans are just pulses.
explanation.definitionFit: To be repulsed is to be driven back or rejected, a synonym of being spurned.

clue.text: Still concerned with a wrong

parts.note: re means about or regarding
a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: Someone is still preoccupied with an injustice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like an adverb but is the noun: a distilling apparatus.
explanation.definitionFit: A retort is a glass vessel with a long neck used for distilling, a kind of laboratory still.

clue.text: In favour of many exercises — and starting in good time

parts.note: pro means for or in support of
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many
PT is physical training

explanation.surface: A supporter of lots of workouts gets going early.
explanation.walkthrough: '— and starting' links the wordplay to the definition, telling us the pieces put together begin punctually.
explanation.definitionFit: Prompt describes something done on time or without delay.

clue.text: A story about a couple of trainees in the city

indicators.note: about means the word for story is placed around the trainees

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story, a fib
L stands for learner, as on a learner driver's plate, so two give LL

explanation.surface: A tale told concerning two apprentices in town.
explanation.definitionFit: Lille is a large city in northern France.

clue.text: Out of jam, say

parts.note: ex is Latin for out of or from
to jam is to press or squeeze

explanation.surface: Someone has run out of preserves, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like 'for example' but is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To express something is to put it into words, to state it.

clue.text: Port doesn't deteriorate

indicators.note: to deteriorate is to fall apart, so the letters of the word before are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A claim that some fortified wine keeps without going off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the wine; it is the Belgian ferry port. The apostrophe in "doesn't" is ignored, leaving DOESNT to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostend is a harbour town on the Belgian coast, a ferry and fishing port.

clue.text: New testament revelation?

indicators.note: New signals that the letters of the next word are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A biblical disclosure, as if from the New Testament or Revelation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Testament' reads as the Bible, and 'revelation' hints at its last book; 'New' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A statement is a declaration or disclosure of facts, something revealed.

clue.text: European schoolboy receiving direction

indicators.note: receiving means the schoolboy takes the compass point inside

parts.note: an Etonian is a pupil at Eton College
S, south, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: A continental pupil is given guidance.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is a famous English boys' school.
explanation.definitionFit: An Estonian is a native of Estonia, a country in Europe.

clue.text: An attractive girl, Eve — and left to get into a mess!

parts.note: a dish is slang for an attractive person
Eve is taken as written

explanation.surface: A pretty young woman and Eve are left in a muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get into a' is link material; 'mess' is the verb, to rumple.
explanation.definitionFit: To dishevel hair or clothes is to make it untidy, to tousle it.

clue.text: Writer dunking bread in drink

indicators.note: in puts the bread inside the word for drink, as if dunked in it

parts.note: to tope is an old word meaning to drink heavily
a roll is a small loaf of bread

explanation.surface: Someone dips their bread into a beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: Anthony Trollope was a Victorian novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Trollope was a nineteenth-century English novelist, author of the Barchester books.

clue.text: Takes a little test as arranged

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of the two words before are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone samples a small quiz that has been organised.
explanation.definitionFit: To taste food is to sample a small amount of it.

clue.text: Call a halt to stone work

parts.note: st is the abbreviation for stone, a British weight
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Someone demands that masonry work ceases.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British unit of weight, 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop something is to bring it to an end.

clue.text: Substitute for military personnel now

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
the present is the time now

explanation.surface: A call for replacement soldiers to be sent immediately.
explanation.definitionFit: To represent someone is to stand in or act on their behalf, taking their place.

clue.text: He sees point in backing Ireland

indicators.note: in puts the compass point inside the name for Ireland
backing means the whole construction is read in reverse order

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A man finds some merit in supporting the Irish team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns EINRE (N inside EIRE) round. 'sees' only links the man to the wordplay; 'point' is a compass point, not a purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernie is a man's given name, so it can stand for an unnamed male person.

clue.text: One gets an encore — or the bird!

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
bis is a call for a repeat performance, an encore

explanation.surface: A performer either gets called back for more or is jeered off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The bird' suggests being booed off stage, but here it is a real bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibis is a long-legged wading bird with a curved bill.

clue.text: Repeatedly striking and playing cricket without hesitation

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the cricket word goes around the hesitation

parts.note: batting is taking a turn at the crease in cricket
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: Someone keeps hitting while playing cricket without pausing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without hesitation' reads as 'unhesitatingly', but 'without' means outside here.
explanation.definitionFit: Battering means hitting hard again and again.

clue.text: Talk about the Spanish church dignitary

indicators.note: about means the word for talk goes around the Spanish article

parts.note: to prate is to chatter on idly
el is the Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: Gossip concerning a senior churchman from Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A prelate is a high-ranking cleric such as a bishop.

clue.text: A contest for people after a home

indicators.note: after puts the people word following the home word

parts.note: a flat is an apartment, a home
a race is a people or nation

explanation.surface: Competition for residents seeking somewhere to live.
explanation.walkthrough: A flat race is a horse race with no jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat race is a horse race run without hurdles or fences.

clue.text: In a stage presentation it creates quite a stir

indicators.note: In says the word it goes inside the rearranged letters
a presentation sets things out in a new form, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A theatre production causes a sensation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'presentation' turns A STAGE into AGATES, and 'In' puts IT inside that.
explanation.definitionFit: To agitate is to stir up or disturb, causing commotion.

clue.text: Brighter, yet more frivolous

definitions.meaning: giving off more illumination, less dark

explanation.surface: Someone is described as cheerier yet less serious.
explanation.definitionFit: Lighter means both paler or more luminous and more light-hearted or trivial.

clue.text: This sounds just the resort for equestrians

indicators.note: sounds says the word for what riders do is said aloud

parts.note: a ride is what equestrians go out on

explanation.surface: A seaside town said to be ideal for horse riders.
explanation.walkthrough: Ryde is a seaside resort on the Isle of Wight, off England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Ryde is a holiday town on the Isle of Wight, a seaside resort.

clue.text: Go off with a list of duties

parts.note: to rot is to decay or go bad

explanation.surface: A worker leaves taking the schedule of chores.
explanation.definitionFit: A rota is a schedule saying who does which task and when.

clue.text: The man who would take stock of other guys

definitions.text: The man who would take stock of other guys

parts.words: The man who would take stock of other guys
parts.note: taking stock sounds like an inventory, but here it is stealing others' livestock

explanation.surface: Someone who would assess other people.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustler is a thief of cattle or horses.

clue.text: A minister's standard issue

parts.note: par is the normal level, the standard
issue means offspring, such as a son

explanation.surface: A government minister's usual handout.
explanation.definitionFit: A parson is a clergyman, a minister of religion.

clue.text: Trains in side-turning? Rubbish!

indicators.note: in puts the trains abbreviation inside the rearranged word
turning means the letters of the word side are churned into a new order

parts.note: BR is British Rail, the former UK railway

explanation.surface: Trains on a branch line? Nonsense!
explanation.walkthrough: 'side-turning' looks like a side road, but 'turning' is an anagram signal here, giving DEIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Debris is scattered waste or rubble, which is rubbish.

clue.text: A charge — an article's to be written about it

indicators.note: about means the article is written around the other word

parts.note: the is the definite article in grammar

explanation.surface: A fee, with a newspaper piece to be produced on the subject.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' is the grammatical word, not a news story; 'to be written' is surface padding around the container signal 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tithe is a levy, traditionally a tenth of produce paid to the church.

clue.text: Finding underworld boss asleep, may be upset

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god ruling the underworld

indicators.note: may be says the letters of the next word could be rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: Discovering the lord of the dead dozing might be unsettling.
explanation.walkthrough: Dis (Pluto) is a classical name for the underworld's ruler; 'may be' rearranges ASLEEP into PLEASE. 'Finding' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To displease someone is to annoy or offend them.

clue.text: Bent, but made some advance, having a heart

indicators.note: having, with heart, means the loan word holds the letter at its centre

parts.note: lent means advanced money as a loan

explanation.surface: Someone stooped but made some progress, with courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having a heart' puts A in the middle of LENT; 'advance' means a loan.
explanation.definitionFit: Leant means inclined or tilted, so bent over.

clue.text: In Ulster an industrious worker has the edge

parts.note: the ant is proverbially hard-working
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: A diligent labourer in Northern Ireland has an advantage.
explanation.walkthrough: Antrim is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland, part of the historic province of Ulster, so 'In Ulster' points to a place found there.
explanation.definitionFit: Antrim is a county located within the province of Ulster.

clue.text: Detergent for plastic lens care

indicators.note: plastic means pliable or mouldable, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A cleaning solution meant for looking after contact lenses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plastic' looks like a material describing the lenses but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A detergent is a cleaning agent, the same thing as a cleaning product.

clue.text: Turning in nothing, is nervous and colours

indicators.note: Turning says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone who is anxious and does nothing at all turns pale.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'and', but 'and' is only a link: 'colours' alone means a flag. 'in' marks the hidden letters, which 'Turning' then reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: A regiment's or ship's colours are its flag, just as an ensign is a naval flag.

clue.text: Puts on an act in front of nurses

parts.note: pre is a prefix meaning before
to tend is to look after or nurse

explanation.surface: Someone performs a show before the hospital staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nurses' looks like a plural noun but is the verb TENDS.
explanation.definitionFit: To pretend is to feign or make believe, a kind of acting.
